 More than 1.5 million pounds of meat including hot dogs, bacon and deli meat recalled 
 Safety in the food chain: Watchdog raises alarm over food recall process (Source: InvestigateTV) By Amanda Alvarado Published : Oct. 19, 2026 at 10:24 AM EDT | Updated : 15 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google (Gray News) - More than 1.5 million pounds of meat, including hot dogs, kielbasa, deli meat, cocktail franks, bologna, bacon and chicken sausage, have been recalled because the products might have been stored at the wrong temperature, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service.
 More than 1.5 million pounds of meat have been recalled because the products might have been stored at the wrong temperature, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service. (U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service) The recalled products were sold under names including Kayem, Specialty Products, Al Fresco, Triple M, McKenzie, Deutschmacher, Jordan’s, Essem and Winnisimmet. The recalled items were produced between March 31 and Oct. 7.
 There have been no reports of illness after consuming the recalled products, and anyone who is concerned should reach out to their doctor.
 Anyone with the recalled products should throw them away or return them to the store where they were purchased.
 A complete list of recalled items can be found here and photos of the recalled items can be found here .
